sections.html:
Newport News is an independent city on the Virginia Peninsula, along the north shore of the James River where it opens into Hampton Roads. It borders James City County, York County and Hampton by land, and shares water borders with several cities across the river.

The city covers 119.63 square miles, and 42.3 percent of that is water. Elevation averages about 15 feet. The 2020 census counted 186,247 residents and the 2025 estimate is 183,230, which makes Newport News the fifth-largest city in Virginia.

Like other Virginia cities, it has no county above it, so city offices handle assessments, tax bills and permits.

sections.h2: How did Newport News become one city with Warwick?
sections.html:
Newport News was a rural area and fishing village until the railroad arrived. In 1881 Collis P. Huntington's Peninsula Extension of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railway opened a way to bring coal to port, and a large shipyard followed within a few years. The city was incorporated in 1896.

The city annexed Kecoughtan in 1927. In 1958, voters agreed to merge Newport News with Warwick, which brought the two places back to roughly their pre-1896 footprint. That is why parts of the city still carry Warwick names.

Much of the city later grew westward, where land was available and highways were built. The older downtown went through a long decline while the shipyard and coal piers kept working.

The sections below show how these facts relate to a sale.

sections.h2: Which Newport News neighborhoods matter to sellers?
sections.html:
Newport News has many distinct neighborhoods, and some sit in the former City of Warwick. Wikipedia names a long list, including these:

  • North End (Huntington Heights): developed mostly between 1900 and 1935, with many architectural styles and river views. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and the Virginia Landmarks Register.
  • Hilton Village, Denbigh, Port Warwick, Oyster Point and City Center.
  • Lee Hall: at the northwest edge, with its historic railroad station.
  • East End and Southeast: older neighborhoods near downtown and the shipyard.
  • Kiln Creek, Windsor Great Park, Newmarket Village and Riverside.

A house in the North End was built a century ago, while one in Kiln Creek is far newer. Condition, roof age and flood exposure vary between them, so any cash price should come from a look at that exact house.

sections.h2: What do the shipyard and military mean for the local economy?
sections.html:
Newport News depends on shipbuilding and the military. Newport News Shipbuilding, owned by Huntington Ingalls Industries, is the city's largest employer with more than 24,000 workers. Fort Eustis employs over 10,000 and the school system more than 5,000.

The Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility is also in the city and employs over 675 people. Ferguson Enterprises and L-3 Flight International Aviation are among the companies headquartered here, and the Newport News Marine Terminal sits at the end of the CSX rail line.

Christopher Newport University is a public university in the city, and Newport News Public Schools runs five high schools: Denbigh, Heritage, Menchville, Warwick and Woodside.

Shipyard shifts and base assignments can lead to quick moves. A worker who gets a new post or an heir who lives far away may want to close without months of showings.

sections.h2: How does Newport News weather affect a house?
sections.html:
Newport News has a humid subtropical climate with cool to mild winters and hot, humid summers. Snowfall averages 5.8 inches per season. Rain falls on about 117 days a year, and the wettest months are July, August and September.

With 42.3 percent of the city covered by water, many properties are close to the James River, creeks or low ground. Wikipedia notes that the city's position tends to be south of the usual path of northern storms and north of the usual tracks of hurricanes, but a storm can still bring heavy rain.

Sellers should ask their insurance agent for flood zone information, and pull any elevation certificate they hold, before signing a contract. The city's Geohub and the FEMA Map Service Center are places to start. Ask the city planning office about any local floodplain rule for your lot.

sections.h2: How are Newport News properties assessed and taxed?
sections.html:
The Real Estate Assessor's Office values each parcel annually, effective the following July 1. City Council decides the real estate tax rate, and the City Treasurer sends bills and collects payment.

The Assessor's Office site lists the department's authority as the Virginia Constitution, state statutes, the Newport News Charter and the city code. The office interprets laws on assessments and exemptions, publishes an annual land book and reviews assessments with owners.

This guide does not list the current tax rate or the bill due dates. Ask the Assessor or the Treasurer for the current numbers before you set a closing date, since an unpaid bill is settled from the sale proceeds.

sections.h2: How do people get around Newport News?
sections.html:
Interstate 64 is the main east and west road, and it links the city to the rest of Hampton Roads through the Hampton Roads Beltway. The Beltway crosses the harbor on two bridge-tunnels, and the James River Bridge and the Monitor-Merrimac Memorial Bridge-Tunnel carry Interstate 664 along the waterfront.

Newport News/Williamsburg International Airport lies partly inside the city. Norfolk International Airport and Richmond International Airport also serve people here. A house close to the interstate or the bridges suits commuters, though it can also mean more road noise, which a buyer may raise.

sections.h2: What does it take to sell a Newport News house for cash?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Newport News follows the same Virginia deed process as any other sale, minus lender approval. The steps are the following.

  • Collect the deed, the latest tax bill and any loan payoff letters.
  • Check the flood zone and any unpermitted work.
  • Pick a settlement company that will search title.
  • Agree on a closing date and sign.

Virginia's grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of value and is paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. The price must appear on the first page of the deed before it can be recorded. Your settlement agent can calculate the total.

sections.h2: What do Newport News sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here run into a few repeat issues.

  • Older houses in the North End, East End or Hilton Village with aging systems.
  • Properties near water with moisture or flood concerns.
  • Rental houses with tenants and deferred repairs.
  • Inherited houses with heirs who live out of state.

A direct sale lets you skip repairs and showings and choose the date.

faqs.q: Is Newport News part of a county?
faqs.a: No. Newport News is an independent city, and it borders James City County, York County and Hampton.

faqs.q: Who sets the Newport News property tax rate?
faqs.a: City Council sets the rate. The Assessor's Office values property, and the City Treasurer sends bills and collects the tax.

faqs.q: How often are Newport News properties assessed?
faqs.a: Every parcel is assessed annually, with the value effective the following July 1, according to the Real Estate Assessor's Office.

faqs.q: What happened when Newport News and Warwick merged?
faqs.a: Voters approved a consolidation in 1958, and the combined city took the name Newport News. Some neighborhoods are still described as part of the former Warwick.

faqs.q: Do I need to fix my Newport News house before selling?
faqs.a: No. A house can be sold as is, though the buyer may price in the condition. Gather any permits and flood paperwork first, because a buyer will ask for them.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia grantor tax?
faqs.a: The seller does unless the contract moves it to the buyer. The rate is 50 cents per $500 of value under Virginia Code 58.1-802.
